author: /root/fork_ownership
scope: The five-file additive checked-release API is safe to integrate while native fork admission/ACK remain disabled. Review covers the changed API, public wrappers/bridge, C fallback selection, exact decrement interpretation, final callback lifetimes and retained actual-body regressions. It does not certify the broader fork transaction or native runtime.

findings.subject: Checked validation and decrement
findings.evidence: Both languages validate the required callbacks and live cached VM/proc fields before decrement. Each new helper consumes at most one selected reference. Exact decrement 0 returns nonfinal; exact 1 enters teardown; negative propagates; any other positive returns -EINVAL. Neither checked helper uses the old dec!=0 predicate. Missing mandatory callback, invalid object and injected error cannot reach final free or final-proof success.

findings.subject: Thread-to-VM completion lifetime
findings.evidence: process_release_thread_checked_body_result caches VM/proc while thread is live, preserves profile/procfs-delete/destroy order, then calls the integer-returning VM callback with only cached VM. It reads neither thread nor VM after that callback. VM result 0 maps to thread 1, VM 1 maps to thread 2, errors propagate and invalid positives reject. Thus result 2 is not produced from a void callback, retained VM or malformed result.

findings.subject: Final VM destruction ordering
findings.evidence: Checked VM teardown preserves the original lock/FD-close/unlock, optional pre-free, flush, memory-range release, address-space detach/process release, policy drainage and final VM free sequence. All mandatory callbacks are validated before decrement. After process release, only the still-live VM policy state is accessed; after free_vm_fn(vm), each implementation returns literal 1 with no further object/field read. Existing pre-free and other teardown callbacks retain their original borrowed-object contracts and are not treated as the final destructor.

findings.subject: Public ABI and fallback selection
findings.evidence: New typed wrappers return the checked helper result and use the same production offsets/callbacks as their legacy counterparts, with the thread wrapper selecting only the new result-returning bridge. Rust supplies matching CInt exports and callback ABI; C definitions/prototypes match. C fallback bodies, wrappers and bridge are selected only without MCKERNEL_RUST_PROCESS_HELPERS, with the corresponding declaration when Rust supplies the bridge. The diff leaves all old body/void-wrapper/bridge definitions unchanged and adds no object field or layout change. Actual native linking remains a later compiler layer.

findings.subject: Scope of completion authority
findings.evidence: The new checked APIs have no kernel/syscall.c caller and do not enable adoption. Non-null CREATE_PPD remains the original -95 gate. Existing void APIs retain their old behavior. A future fork caller must separately prove HostRevoked and use saved scalar identity; only exact checked thread result 2 could authorize ACK. Results 0/1/error give no asynchronous completion, rollback or pointer-retry authority.

languages: Rust 1.92 actual bodies linked to the same C adapters
actual_body_execution.coverage: Retained source checks freeze ten old C/Rust body/wrapper/bridge regions, three C structure regions and the Rust layout hash; check additive prototype/offset/fallback selection and closed gate. Executable vectors distinguish thread nonfinal, thread final/VM nonfinal, both final, direct VM outcomes, optional callbacks/lists, every required callback omission, null fields, decrement 0/1/-5/2 and VM callback -5/2. The same adapter runs and asserts expected results/traces for C and Rust, then compares their reports. Scalar-only caller vectors require HostRevoked/identity before one release and ACK only exact result 2.
actual_body_execution.post_free_detector: Destroy-thread, process-release and final-VM-free callbacks mprotect separate own pages PROT_NONE. A subsequent field read by either actual body would fault. Two independent child reads prove protected-page reads terminate SIGSEGV. Nondumpable guards run before suite assertions and protected accesses and are repeated in each child; guard failure exits 86 and cannot satisfy the signal oracle.
actual_body_execution.limits: Helpers execute verbatim, but object layouts, refcounts, FD/policy operations, kernel locks and concrete destructor bridges are adapters. Public wrappers are source/ABI checked rather than executed against the real kernel. Protected pages detect memory reads, not kernel TLB retirement or guest teardown. No native build, real VM destruction, host-revoke proof, guest ACK or application acceptance follows from this fixture.

history_preserved: The author record retains the corrected original C-bridge baseline extraction and original dumpable fixture/profile side-effect finding. This review uses the corrected exact profile/source hashes and successful central execution; it neither erases failures nor resets their family history.
integration_decision: Integrate the additive checked APIs and their retained tests under the dispatcher's normal source/compiler workflow. Keep old APIs unchanged and all fork admission/ACK integration disabled. No repeat compiler run or broader fork design review is required to resolve this source review.
campaign_scope: Reviewer wrote only this new evidence file and made no implementation, compiler, Git, root, Docker, guest or network changes. Image candidate fd099 and the independent image-first critical path remain untouched.
